column1: Even the earliest of tribes had a system of numeration that, if not advanced, was sufficient for the tasks that they had to perform.

column1: However, when early humans first began to reflect on the nature of things around them, they discovered that they needed an idea of number simply to keep their thoughts in order.

column1: As they began to settle, grow plants and herd animals, the need for a sophisticated number system became paramount.

column1: It will never be known how and when this numeration ability developed, but it is certain that numeration was well developed by the time humans had formed even semi-permanent settlements.
column2: 这种计数能力是怎样、又是在何时形成的，我们永远无从得知。但有一点可以肯定：早在人类形成哪怕只是半永久性的定居点时，计数就已相当发达。

column1: The indigenous peoples of Tasmania were only able to count one, two, many; those of South Africa counted one, two, two and one, two twos, two twos and one, and so on.
column2: 塔斯马尼亚的原住民只能数「一、二、许多」。南非的原住民则数「一、二、二加一、两个二、两个二加一」，以此类推。

column1: But in real situations the number and words are often accompanied by gestures to help resolve any confusion.

column1: This basic approach is limited in the range of numbers that it can express, but this range will generally suffice when dealing with the simpler aspects of human existence.

column1: Perhaps the most fundamental step in developing a sense of number is not the ability to count, but rather to see that a number is really an abstract idea instead of a simple attachment to a group of particular objects.
column2: 形成数感最根本的一步，也许不在于能够数数，而在于认识到数其实是一个抽象概念，并不只是附属于某一组具体事物的特征。

column1: The numeration system of the Tsimshian language in British Columbia contains seven distinct sets of words for numbers according to the class of the item being counted: for counting flat objects and animals, for round objects and time, for people, for long objects and trees, for canoes, for measures, and for counting when no particular object is being numerated.
column2: 在不列颠哥伦比亚省的钦西安语中，数词按所数对象的类别分为七套：一套数扁平物体和动物，一套数圆形物体和时间，一套数人，一套数长条物体和树木，一套数独木舟，一套用于度量，最后一套用于单纯数数而不特指任何东西。

column1: It seems that the last is a later development while the first six groups show the relics of an older system.
